Ecopetrol SA Unveils New Sustainable Fuel Product in Colombia

Bogotá—In a move aimed at advancing Colombia's energy transition, Ecopetrol SA, the country’s leading oil and gas producer, announced the launch of its new sustainable fuel product on Thursday. The new fuel, named EcoAdvance, was unveiled at a press event held at the company’s research and development center in Barrancabermeja, Santander.

EcoAdvance is designed to reduce carbon emissions and improve engine efficiency in both commercial and private transport sectors. According to Ecopetrol SA, the product is the result of four years of research and collaboration with Colombian universities and local engineering firms, including Innovar Combustibles. Developed with a blend of bio-components sourced from Colombian agricultural producers, the fuel aims to provide a viable alternative as the nation seeks cleaner energy solutions.

“We are proud to introduce EcoAdvance as part of our commitment to the country’s sustainable future,” said María Fernanda Suárez, Ecopetrol SA’s Vice President of Innovation and Technology. “This product supports our goal to lower the carbon footprint of our operations and those of our clients, while also promoting local supply chains.”

Industry observers have welcomed the announcement. “This is an important step for Colombia’s oil and gas sector,” said Andrés Cárdenas, an analyst at the Colombian Association of Energy Professionals. “Ecopetrol’s investment in lower-emission fuels demonstrates leadership and responsiveness to global trends in energy demand.”

The company noted that EcoAdvance will initially be distributed at select service stations in Bogotá, Medellín, and Cali, with plans to expand availability nationwide by the end of the year. The fuel is compatible with existing vehicle engines and infrastructure, facilitating an easy transition for consumers.

Local suppliers also expressed optimism. “Our partnership with Ecopetrol has opened new opportunities for small-scale farmers in the region,” remarked Luz Marina Torres, director of the Santander Agricultural Cooperative. “Supplying raw materials for EcoAdvance strengthens rural economies and supports sustainable farming.”

Ecopetrol SA projects that the introduction of EcoAdvance could reduce annual carbon emissions by up to 120,000 tons once fully adopted in major cities. The company pledged ongoing investment in research and development to further expand its portfolio of clean energy products in the coming years.
